2026-11-11.title: Wednesday of the Thirty-second Week in Ordinary Time · St Martin of Tours, Bishop
readings: He saved us by the water of rebirth
The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want
Only one returned to give thanks
2026-11-11.alt: Memorial of St Martin of Tours, bishop.
2026-11-11.verse: Then one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, praising God with a loud voice. He prostrated himself at Jesus' feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
theo: Ten lepers cry out from a distance, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!” Jesus sends them to the priests, and on the way they are cleansed. All ten are healed; only one comes back, praising God aloud and falling at Jesus' feet. He is a Samaritan, a foreigner. Jesus tells him: “Your faith has made you well,” literally “has saved you”. Ten received healing; one received salvation, because he turned back to the Healer.

Paul tells Titus that God “saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit”. Baptism is our cleansing; gratitude is our turning back. St Martin of Tours, a soldier who shared his cloak with a beggar and later became a monk and bishop, lived out that gratitude in mercy toward the poor.
outline: Ask: how many of your prayers this week were requests, and how many were thanks?
Like the lepers, we are healed by grace, through Baptism.
Point 3 · Faith that saves and serves
St Martin's cloak: thanks becomes mercy.
live: Spend five minutes tonight only thanking God.
Give a garment or blanket to someone in need this week.
2026-11-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, you have cleansed me in the waters of Baptism. Let me not be like the nine who forgot, but turn back each day to thank you, and like St Martin share what I have with the poor. Amen.

quick: Ten were healed; one turned back and was saved.
We are saved by mercy, through the water of rebirth.
2026-11-11.action: Spend five minutes only thanking God.
2026-11-11.question: Have I thanked God for my Baptism?

homily: Dear friends, ten lepers stood at a distance and cried out: Jesus, Master, have mercy on us. Jesus sent them to the priests, and on the way they were cleansed (Luke 17:12–14). All ten were healed. Only one came back, praising God with a loud voice and falling at Jesus' feet, and he was a Samaritan, a foreigner.

Jesus asks: were not ten made clean? Where are the other nine? And to the one who returned he says: your faith has made you well (Luke 17:17–19), or, as the word also means, has saved you. Ten received healing; one received salvation, because he came back to the Healer.

Paul reminds Titus that God saved us not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). Everything begins with mercy, and mercy received calls for thanks.

Today we remember St Martin of Tours, the soldier who shared his cloak with a beggar and saw Christ wearing it that night. Gratitude turned into generosity. Let us keep a list this week: three thanks each night, and one act of mercy each day. Amen.
kids: Children, only one leper said thank you to Jesus. Let us be like him! Tonight, tell Jesus three things you are thankful for.

intro: Cleansed by mercy, we turn back in thanks, and thanks becomes mercy.

sub: The lepers cried from a distance.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were made clean.

sub: Nine took the gift and went.
One came back to the Giver.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits.
Then one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, praising God with a loud voice. He prostrated himself at Jesus' feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
points.apply: Make your next prayer only thanksgiving.

sub: He saw Christ in the beggar.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
points.apply: Give a garment to someone in need.

concl: Grace received calls for grace returned.
Be the one who comes back.
2026-11-11.resolve: Keep a gratitude list this week: three thanks each night.
